**If you’re a UK sole trader and most customers pay by bank transfer, I’d choose Starling’s Sole Trader account.** There’s no monthly fee, you can create and send invoices for free, and you can set money aside for tax. It also connects to Xero, QuickBooks and FreeAgent without a bank integration fee. The main drawback is cash: Post Office deposits cost **0.7%, with a £3 minimum per deposit**, and sole traders can deposit at most **£20,000 per calendar year**. ([starlingbank.com](https://www.starlingbank.com/sole-trader-bank-account/))

I’d change that recommendation in three situations:

| If this describes your business | I’d choose | Why |
|---|---|---|
| You’re starting out and want branch access or your accountant uses FreeAgent | **NatWest Start-up** | For eligible businesses trading less than a year with turnover under £1m, everyday banking is free for two years. FreeAgent stays free while you keep the account, but standard transaction charges apply after year two. ([natwest.com](https://www.natwest.com/business/bank-accounts/startup-bank-account.html?intcam=HP-B-P3-DEF-Default&utm_source=openai)) |
| You’re a sole trader or run a one-person limited company and just need a basic account | **Monzo Business Lite** | No monthly fee and free UK bank transfers. I’d start with Lite rather than pay **£9/month for Pro**, unless you specifically want features such as automatically setting aside tax or invoicing from Monzo. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/business-banking/plans-pricing)) |
| You have employees who need to spend company money | **Monzo Business Team** | From **£25/month**, it offers employee expense cards with spending limits and bulk payments for salaries or suppliers. Those are concrete reasons to pay for an account rather than use a free one. ([monzo.com](https://monzo.com/business-banking/plans-pricing)) |

One UK distinction: a **sole trader** doesn’t legally need a business account, though some personal accounts prohibit business use. A **limited company** must keep its banking separate from the directors’ personal banking. ([business.gov.uk](https://www.business.gov.uk/support/accounting-tax-cashflow/getting-a-business-bank-account/?utm_source=openai))

If you regularly take cash, **how much you deposit and how often** matters more than the monthly fee: at Starling, paying in £100 four times costs £12, versus £3 for one £400 deposit. If you tell me whether you’re a sole trader or Ltd, how customers usually pay, and whether you already use accounting software, I can narrow this to one account. ([help.starlingbank.com](https://help.starlingbank.com/business/topics/cash-and-cheques/can-i-deposit-cash-into-my-account/?utm_source=openai))
